---

Our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms (5–7 November, Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune) wrapped up on Saturday, and I think it worked.

41 participants from 9 states, mostly MSc and early-PhD students, out of 112 applications. We shortlisted on the strength of a statement and one reference, and I am glad we did. For most of them this was a first close look at the research frontier, and the questions in the sessions were sharp.

The academic programme was carried by three speakers we are grateful to: Dr Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) on Mordell-Weil groups, Dr Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) on modular forms, and Dr Tomasz Wierzbicki, joining us online from Kraków, on computations in Sage. Our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, shaped the schedule and kept us honest. The problem sessions run by our PhD students worked far better than we expected, and I would keep that format for any future edition.

Two moments I will not forget. On day two the power failed for nearly two hours and most laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen, pulled out two rolling whiteboards, and honestly, that turned into the best session of the three days. Small schools like this matter more than the big conferences, because an MSc student can actually stop a speaker and ask why.

Second, a participant from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes. She corrected it live, thanked him, and the whole room watched a mistake become a lesson.

The Rs 2.4 lakh from the institute's student initiative grant covered hostel accommodation and travel for 18 outstation students. Mr Prakash Salunke from the office sorted out a hostel booking mess at 11pm and made it look effortless. Six PhD volunteers handled the TA work without a hitch. Thank you.

Slides and problem sheets will be on the department website within two weeks.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, if the grant comes through. If you applied and did not make it this time, please apply again.

On behalf of Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza and me: thank you.

#EllipticCurves #ModularForms #NumberTheory
